PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.

items.rationale: The theft-damaged frame is covered at the cost of a comparable replacement under 2.3.1(b) and 7.1.7(b). The €3,500 agreed value replaces the €500 class cap under 4.4; it is a ceiling, not a flat payment.
Sections 7.1.7(b) and 7.1.9 cover equivalent brakes at the pre-theft grade. The estimate allows €90 per brake for two brakes, excluding separately billed fitting.

Section 7.1.7(f) expressly covers necessary freight for replacement parts or transport of the damaged bike for repair. The estimate allows one standard shipment for the repair, provided it does not duplicate a vehicle charge.

Sections 7.1.7(g) and 7.1.8(f) cover one necessary repair attendance, but the claim specifically documents only the locksmith's visit. If the bicycle service trip was separately required, the allowance is €77.

Section 7.1.7(c) covers fitting, alignment and testing after frame and brake replacement. The €109 allowance is for assembly distinct from the separately billed hours, as duplicate costs are excluded by 7.1.8(g).
Section 7.1.7(e) covers a modest allowance for fixings and consumables used in the covered repair. The generic description leaves some uncertainty because 7.1.8(d) excludes shop overhead and tools.
Section 7.1.7(d) expressly covers necessary apprentice labour. The estimate is one hour at €36, provided it is not already billed in the assembly charge.
Section 7.1.7(d) covers necessary skilled labour at customary rates, and 7.1.8(g) excludes duplicate billing. The estimate allows one distinct skilled hour at €79.
Section 5.2.2(a) covers the locksmith's necessary attendance where the bicycle was found. One trip at €39 follows the close locksmith reference; the €1,000 recovery cap does not reduce it.

Under 7.1.10, the purpose of the charge controls: if this is the flat-rate operation to release the bicycle, 5.2.2(b) covers it at €109. Fitting a new lock or duplicating the same labour would not qualify as recovery.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers materials actually consumed in cutting off the lock, but 7.1.8(d) excludes the locksmith's own tools and overhead. If substantiated as consumables, the allowance is €8.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers every labour grade used to release the bicycle. One apprentice hour is allowed at €36, consistent with the close reference.

Section 5.2.2(b) covers skilled lock-removal labour, but 7.1.8(g) bars charging it again if included in the flat-rate operation. The estimate allows €42 for separately justified skilled work on the brief release.
